title: Campaign: non-invasive brain measurement, magnetic resonance contrasts
abstract: Subcampaign of 'how can human brain activity be measured without surgery, better than today?'. Scope: Nuclear magnetic resonance signals: BOLD and its physics, neural-current MRI (spin-lock), sodium and xenon MRI, susceptibility, diffusion, and electrical-property tomography. Elastography is in the coupled branch. 34 papers. Status: several proposed contrasts fail. In cortical models, neural-current fields are 14-1300 times below what published phase-agnostic spin-lock MRI tests at 3 T can detect, while a phase-referenced readout could detect alpha in about 1 h; in rodent cortex models one forepaw pulse changes the sodium MRI signal by about 0.02-0.25% (medians) against a reported 2-3%; an ADC decrease in BOLD-active cortex was not found and circular voxel selection and b-value ordering can produce the published decrease; bSSFP functional-conductivity phase is at most about one fifth explained by BOLD, and in folded-cortex models the functional EPT phase signal comes mostly from blood displacing CSF. Diffusion and exchange designs show vascular confounds that robust protocols reduce.
